correctness.rationale: Domination iff all rows or all columns hit; minimum-removal test classifies maximum cardinality n as exactly one token in each column while missing some row. Any legal one-token move stays within its column, proving jumps=slides and induced non-surjective ternary Hamming graph. Inclusion-exclusion gives 3*2^n-3, degree sum gives 3n(2^{n-1}+1). Reconstructed constructive upper paths for constant/single-shared support words and first-extinction lower witness a^n vs b^k c^{n-k} to prove n+k-1. Independent all-pairs BFS for n=4,5,6,7 verified vertex/edge counts and diameters 5,6,8,9; finite checks only corroborate proof.

originality.rationale: Brešar 2005 provides general upper-domination product inequality, not optimum-space reconfiguration. Suzuki-Mouawad-Nishimura 2014 investigate adding/removing domination tokens with budget rather than fixed-size inclusion-minimal max-sets. Complexity and integer-programming sources also do not imply this exact ternary word-state graph and diameter. Searched alias non-surjective words and rook reconfiguration; no direct prior equivalence found.
